title: The Abyss Where Echoes Learn Restraint

features.name: the shed of absorption
features.desc-on-touch: You find an underground storage shed, its walls lined with decades of foam and fibre. The silence inside is so complete it sounds like pressure. You can feel the echo that could have been but never was.

features.name: the restraint pool
features.desc-on-touch: Water fills a basin carved into bedrock. The surface is perfectly still — any sound dies before it touches the mirror. This is what echo learns when it finally stops trying to be heard.

features.name: the archive's listening post
features.desc-on-touch: An old broadcast casing sits half-buried, its antenna rusted silent. Once it spoke to every tree in the network. Now it just collects the sound that nobody needs to hear.

features.name: the measurement that never echoed
features.desc-on-touch: A plaque of unreadable writing marks the point where the abyss begins. The engraving is so fine that light itself seems reluctant to reflect from it.

features.name: the deepening shaft
features.desc-on-touch: A vertical passage descends beyond sight. Your voice reaches down and down and down and then — nothing. The sound has learned to keep going, not to return.

inscription: here the sound learns that the only way to truly speak is to stop speaking and begin listening to what the earth was trying to say all along

file.name: AcousticAbsorption_TestRecordings_1987.wav
file.note: Early attempts to measure how sound dies in bedrock chambers. Each recording gets quieter. The last one is silence.
